replacement: Sweet Beatrice, would you come when I called you?
BEATRICE. In spite of your heart, I think. Alas, poor heart! If you spite it for my sake, I'll spite it for yours. I will never love what my friend hates.

BENEDICK. Good question. Why, an hour of noise and a quarter of an hour of tears. So it's most sensible for a wise man—if Don Worm, his conscience, sees no objection—to be the trumpet of his own virtues, as I am for myself. That's enough about praising myself, who, I'll testify myself, deserve praise. And now tell me, how is your cousin?

CLAUDIO. I had hoped you'd turn Beatrice down, so I could beat you with a club out of your single life and make you a double-dealer, both a married man and a cheat. Without doubt you will be one, if my cousin doesn't watch you very closely.
